issues.description: The Bitmap24::set method has inconsistent parameter naming between its declaration and definition: the header declares parameters as (int i_x, int i_y, ...) suggesting (x, y) order, while the implementation defines the function as set(int i_y, int i_x, ...) and uses the first parameter as the row and the second as the column. This mismatch between the header's parameter names and the implementation's names is likely to confuse students about the intended coordinate order (row vs column) when calling bitmap.set(...), even though the types match. It increases cognitive load and risks incorrect usage or misunderstanding of the API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter names and their intended semantic order consistent between declaration and definition. For example, change the declaration in Bitmap24.hpp to set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) or rename parameters to explicit names like set(int row, int col, char r, char g, char b) in both the header and implementation, and update any documentation/comments to clarify that the first parameter is the row (y) and the second is the column (x).
